4.2.1.3.rationale: Aconitase catalyzes a single isomerization (citrate <-> isocitrate via cis-aconitate); cytosolic aconitase doubles as iron regulatory protein-1 (IRP1), an RNA-binding moonlighting role, not a second catalytic activity.
4.2.1.3.evidence: PMID:39337438 (review of mitochondrial/cytosolic aconitase functions, describes IRP1 moonlighting as RNA-binding, not catalytic)

5.3.1.9.rationale: Glucose-6-phosphate isomerase performs one isomerase reaction; its extracellular 'neuroleukin'/autocrine motility factor role is a non-catalytic signaling/moonlighting function, matching the hexokinase-type exclusion criterion.
5.3.1.9.evidence: PMID:35135854 (describes 'neurotrophic function of Glucose-6-Phosphate Isomerase', a moonlighting cytokine-like role, no second EC activity)

6.2.1.7.rationale: Bile acid-CoA ligase (cholate:CoA ligase) is a single-activity acyl-CoA synthetase; no literature was found describing a fused second catalytic domain.

6.3.2.11.rationale: Carnosine synthase (identified as ATP-grasp domain-containing protein ATPGD1) is a single ATP-grasp ligase forming one amide bond (AMP-forming); no second catalytic activity is reported.
6.3.2.11.evidence: PMID:20097752 (molecular identification of carnosine synthase as ATPGD1, single ligase activity)

1.1.1.119.rationale: Glucose 1-dehydrogenase (NADP+) is a simple single-activity sugar dehydrogenase; no literature describing a fused second catalytic activity was found.

1.1.1.120.rationale: Galactose dehydrogenase (NADP+) is a single-activity sugar dehydrogenase; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found.

1.1.1.124.rationale: Mannitol 2-dehydrogenase (NAD+) performs a single oxidoreductase reaction; searches returned only pathway-context reviews mentioning the enzyme as one step among many, not evidence of a fused second activity.

1.1.1.138.rationale: This mannitol dehydrogenase (distinct stereospecific isoform from 1.1.1.124) likewise shows no literature evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.146.rationale: 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (cortisol/cortisone interconversion) is a well-characterized single-activity SDR enzyme; the bidirectional dehydrogenase/reductase behavior of HSD11B1 is the same EC-type reaction run in either direction, not a second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.181.rationale: 7alpha-hydroxysteroid/7alpha-hydroxycholesterol dehydrogenase performs a single oxidoreductase reaction in bile-acid metabolism; no credible literature links this specific enzyme to a fused second catalytic domain (an unrelated bifunctional HSD17B4 hit from the search was a keyword coincidence, not about this EC).

1.1.1.195.rationale: Cinnamyl-alcohol/coniferyl-alcohol dehydrogenase (CAD) is a well-studied single-activity lignin-pathway oxidoreductase with no reported fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.222.rationale: Phenyllactate dehydrogenase is a single-activity aromatic 2-hydroxyacid dehydrogenase; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found.

1.1.1.237.rationale: Aromatic-lactate dehydrogenase (phenyllactate dehydrogenase family member) is a single-activity oxidoreductase; no fused second catalytic activity reported in the literature.

1.1.1.246.rationale: Medicarpin reductase (plant pterocarpan biosynthesis) is a single-activity NADPH-dependent reductase; no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity was found.

1.1.1.297.rationale: Menthol/menthane-diol dehydrogenase is a single-activity terpenoid oxidoreductase; no literature on a fused second catalytic activity was found (zero relevant hits).

1.1.1.307.rationale: Xylitol dehydrogenase (NADP+) is a single-activity sugar-alcohol oxidoreductase; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found.

1.1.1.53.rationale: 3alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (B-specific) is a single-activity SDR/AKR-family steroid oxidoreductase; no literature describing a fused second catalytic activity was found.

1.1.1.62.rationale: Estradiol 17beta-dehydrogenase activity (EC 1.1.1.62) is carried by several single-domain SDR isozymes (e.g. HSD17B1/2/6); although a related family member (HSD17B4/MFE-2, 'D-bifunctional protein') genuinely fuses a 17beta-HSD-like dehydrogenase domain with an enoyl-CoA hydratase domain, no literature was found directly assigning EC 1.1.1.62 itself to that bifunctional protein, so the default monofunctional call applies to this EC.
1.1.1.62.evidence: PMID:20673864 (describes HSD17B4/DBP as a distinct bifunctional peroxisomal protein, but not co-cited with EC 1.1.1.62)

1.1.3.9.rationale: Galactose oxidase is a single-activity copper radical oxidase; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found (zero relevant hits).

1.1.99.18.rationale: Cellobiose dehydrogenase is a two-domain flavocytochrome (FAD dehydrogenase domain plus heme b cytochrome domain), but the heme domain functions as an internal electron-transfer relay to external acceptors rather than carrying an independent, classically EC-assigned catalytic activity, so the enzyme catalyzes one overall reaction (cellobiose:acceptor 1-oxidoreductase).
1.1.99.18.evidence: PMID:23329127 (describes the flavocytochrome two-domain architecture of CDH as a single biocatalyst, not two distinct catalytic activities)

1.10.3.1.rationale: Catechol oxidase (diphenol oxidase) is a single-activity type-3 copper oxidase; no literature describing a fused second catalytic activity was found.

1.11.1.6.rationale: Standard catalase (EC 1.11.1.6) catalyzes H2O2 dismutation as its sole classified activity; the genuinely bifunctional catalase-peroxidase (KatG) is a distinct enzyme under a different EC number (1.11.1.21), not this one.
1.11.1.6.evidence: none found specific to EC 1.11.1.6 fusion with a second catalytic domain, defaulted to monofunctional

1.14.11.23.rationale: Flavonol synthase (a 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase) is reported to show catalytic promiscuity/overlap with flavanone 3-hydroxylase (F3H) activity at a single active site in some plants, but this is substrate promiscuity of one domain rather than a literature-established fused second catalytic domain, so it remains monofunctional by the stated criteria.
1.14.11.23.evidence: 28 EuropePMC hits on FLS/F3H dual activity describe single-active-site catalytic promiscuity, not domain fusion; defaulted to monofunctional

1.14.13.112.rationale: Sterol C-23 hydroxylase (brassinosteroid biosynthesis, cytochrome P450-type monooxygenase) is a single-activity enzyme; no bifunctional/multifunctional literature was found.

1.14.13.124.rationale: Phenylalanine N-monooxygenase (CYP79-type, N-hydroxylating/decarboxylating, glucosinolate biosynthesis) is a single-activity P450 enzyme; no literature on a fused second catalytic activity was found.
